11.26.0.en: St. Philoxenus "The liberal soul shall be made fat: and he that watereth shall be watered also himself" [25]

11.26.1.en: He who is generous, especially toward the needy and the suffering, in pure love, receives from God a hundredfold of God's mercies in this world.

11.26.2.en: God is wonderful, for He has given us everything, and also gives us generosity of soul and breadth of heart so that we may use what He has given us in a fitting way, and He returns and repays us a hundredfold because of our response to His gift to us.

11.26.3.en: Love waters the souls of others, and God in His love waters our thirsty souls.

11.26.4.en: * "Every blessed soul is simple [25 LXX], does not cling to temporal things, and is not brought low with wings unspread, but shines with the splendor of the virtues, soars in the open air on the twofold wings of love (for God and for the neighbor), and sees how to offer to others that in which it strives, and is not in idle rest, but says in security: 'The Lord gave, the Lord hath taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord, let Him do according to His good pleasure!'"

11.26.5.en: St. Augustine * He says: "The soul that blesses is made fat, and he that watereth shall be watered also himself" [25]. For he who blesses from without by preaching receives within the fatness of an enlarged (heart), and while he does not cease to water the minds of his hearers with the wine of eloquence, he is all the more refreshed by the multiplied gift...

11.26.7.en: * May those who hide the word of teaching within them listen in dread to the voice of divine judgment, so that this dread may remove another dread from their hearts (that is, that the dread of judgment may remove the dread of venturing to teach). And let them know that those who do not put forward their gifts lose them and forfeit them; not only do they lose them, but with the loss the curse falls upon them. And let them hear how Paul was confident that he was innocent of the blood of his brothers inasmuch as he did not delay in the effort of rebuking sins. In this he says: "Wherefore I take you to record this day, that I am pure from the blood of all men. For I have not shunned to declare unto you all the counsel of God" (Acts 20:26-27). And let them hear also how the angelic voice warns John, saying: "And let him that heareth say, Come" (Rev 22:17), meaning that those who hear His voice in their depths must also raise their voices to draw others to where God calls them. This is lest, if one of them comes forward empty-handed, he finds the doors shut before him. And then he hears the word of Isaiah, who during the ministry of the word closed his lips, although the heavenly light had shone and lit upon him, and who therefore cries out in repentance, rebuking himself, saying: "Woe is me! for I am undone; because I am a man of unclean lips" (Isa 6:5). And let them hear the words of Solomon which show how the teacher's wisdom increases if he does not hide his gifts through the sin of sluggishness, which say: "The liberal soul shall be made fat: and he that watereth shall be watered also himself" (Prov 11:25). Those who go out to the ministry of teaching distribute its blessings, and so they are filled within and increase. And as long as the teacher continues to water his hearers with the wine of effective spiritual words, the sips of multiplied grace make him drunk. Let them hear how David presented this as a gift from God, and did not hide the gift of teaching which God gave him: "Lo, I have not refrained my lips, O LORD, thou knowest. I have not hid thy righteousness within my heart; I have declared thy faithfulness and thy salvation" (Ps 40:9-10).

11.26.9.en: * "The sway of his wrath is his destruction" (Sir 1:22), "The wrathful man is not beautiful," for there is nothing more shameful or uglier than a face inflamed with anger.

11.27.0.en: St. John Chrysostom "He that withholdeth corn, the people shall curse him: but blessing shall be upon the head of him that selleth it" [26]

11.27.1.en: It is fitting that we not keep the Lord's blessings and gifts to ourselves alone in selfishness, but offer from what we have been given to our brothers. Perhaps what is meant here by hoarding is that a man keeps the wheat and does not sell it, waiting for the price to rise so that he dictates his terms to the buyers.

11.27.2.en: * May the love of money come to an end, may the lust for (wealth) die... To demand an increase in price is a sign of malice, not of simplicity. Therefore it is said: "He who demands a high price for his wheat, the people shall curse him."

11.27.3.en: * Solomon the wise rightly says: "He that withholdeth corn leaves it to the nations," he does not leave it as an inheritance, because he who acquires greed does not work for the good of his successors.

11.27.4.en: St. Ambrose * "He that withholdeth corn, the people shall curse him." He who keeps (the wheat) for himself has no mercy. He does not gather (the wheat) for the sake of mercy. Yet unless he gathers, how can he offer mercy? Is it not also a fact that people bless him who spends and gives? As it is written here and in the pages of the Holy Scriptures?

11.27.5.en: St. Anba Shenouda Pope Gregory (the Great) holds that he who keeps wheat for himself and hoards it is the one who keeps the holy word of preaching for himself, and keeps silent without profiting by it in the correction of others; such a one deserves the curse of the people.

11.27.6.en: * Those who are able to teach with great effect, yet hold back out of excessive humility, should learn to infer, from reflection on small matters, how greatly they sin in the greater and more important tasks. Therefore, if they were to hide from needy brothers the money in their possession, they would doubtless cast sadness and grief upon them. Let them consider how deeply they are involved in a great guilt, for by withholding the word of teaching from sinful brothers, they withhold the medicine of life from souls going to death. Therefore the wise man says rightly: "Wisdom that is hid, and treasure that is hoarded up, what profit is in them both?" (Sir 20:32). If a famine were destroying a people, and this people hid their wheat, they would doubtless be heralds and announcers of death. Accordingly, let those who do not come forward to minister the bread of grace which has been granted them, when souls perish of thirst for the holy word, consider the terror of the punishment. Therefore it is also said rightly by the tongue of Solomon: "He that withholdeth corn, the people shall curse him" (Prov 11:26); he who hides the wheat keeps for himself the words of holy teaching. Such a man is struck by the curse, because by the sin of silence he deserves the punishment of all those who could have walked in what is right because of him.

11.28.0.en: The righteous man does not rely on material wealth, but on genuine righteousness [28]. He inherits rewards that build his house [29], and sees the fruit of his life in souls he leads to the Lord [30].

11.28.1.en: "He that diligently seeketh good procureth favour: but he that seeketh mischief, it shall come unto him" [27]

11.28.2.en: He who strives toward what is good is rewarded according to his sincerity and faithfulness, and finds the favor of others and becomes a cause of their joy. But he who does evil and delights in the troubles of others and in harming them, it returns upon him. As Adonibezek said: "Threescore and ten kings, having their thumbs and their great toes cut off, gathered their meat under my table: as I have done, so God hath requited me" (Judg 1:7). The Apostle says: "Whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap. For he that soweth to his flesh shall of the flesh reap corruption; but he that soweth to the Spirit shall of the Spirit reap life everlasting. And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not. As we have therefore opportunity, let us do good unto all men, especially unto them who are of the household of faith" (Gal 6:7-10).

11.28.3.en: St. John Chrysostom says that it is fitting for us to seize every opportunity to do good, for if the opportunity is lost it may not return again.

11.28.4.en: And Father Marius Victorinus says: [It is not enough to do good, but we must always strive to do good, for many began to do good and stopped, either because they grew tired or strayed from the way. We must not grow weary in doing good, and must continue in it. He also says: [The time is short, and life quickly reaches its end, the end of the world is at the doors. We have opportunity, that is, as long as we are alive or while life still continues in this world.]

11.29.0.en: "He that trusteth in his riches shall fall; but the righteous shall flourish as a branch" [28]

11.29.1.en: The Apostle says: "Charge them that are rich in this world, that they be not highminded, nor trust in uncertain riches, but in the living God, who giveth us richly all things to enjoy; that they do good, that they be rich in good works" (1 Tim 6:17-18).

11.29.2.en: The Lord Christ warns us not to imitate the foolish rich man who said: "This will I do: I will pull down my barns, and build greater; and there will I bestow all my fruits and my goods. And I will say to my soul, Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry" (Lk 12:18-19).

11.29.3.en: * He thought within himself, saying: What shall I do, because I have no room where to bestow my fruits? He said, This will I do: I will pull down my barns, and build greater, and there will I bestow all my fruits and my goods. There is no more trivial position than this. In truth he had pulled down his barns, since the secure storehouses on which he depends are the bellies of the poor, not the walls of the barns...

11.29.4.en: Truly death came, and put out all this luxury, and led him away as a captive with bowed head, groaning with shame, unable to speak, trembling with fear, as though his enjoyment of all this luxury had been a dream.

11.29.5.en: In the end the rich man was reduced to entreating the poor man, begging him, he who had before lain hungry exposed to the mouths of dogs. The situation was reversed, and all knew who was the truly rich and who the truly poor, and so Lazarus became the richest of all and the other the poorest of all. And as it is in the theater, where the actors enter in borrowed masks as kings, generals, physicians, teachers, sages and soldiers, while in reality they are not so, so in the present life poverty and wealth are nothing but masks. For if you sit in the theater and see one of the actors wearing the mask of a king, you do not count him fortunate for that, nor do you believe that he really is a king, nor do you wish to be like him; but because you know that he is a merchant, or perhaps a rope-maker or a barrel-maker or something of the kind, you do not count him fortunate on account of his borrowed mask or the costume he wears, nor judge his social standing by the cheapness of his other garb, for this is not a sign on which you can rely.

11.29.6.en: Here too it is the same: sitting here in the world as though in a theater, and looking at the actors on the stage, you see many rich people, but you do not believe that they are really rich, for they are wearing borrowed masks of the rich.

11.30.0.en: St. John Chrysostom "He that troubleth his own house shall inherit the wind: and the fool shall be servant to the wise of heart" [29]

11.30.1.en: If he who sows a few seeds reaps much at harvest time, and if from a small spark fires arise which may devour thousands of acres, as happens in forests, so he who sows a few evils and bad habits destroys his house, and perhaps his grandchildren's grandchildren, who imitate him with some exaggeration.

11.30.2.en: The second part of the proverb refers to the rich owners of power, who think the lives of others are in their hands, but soon collapse before the wise and devout children of God.

11.30.3.en: Daniel was brought before King Belshazzar, and the latter said to him: "Art thou that Daniel, which art of the children of the captivity of Judah, whom the king my father brought out of Judah?" (Dan 5:13). The same night Belshazzar was slain and the kingdom of Babylon came to an end, while Daniel was honored.

11.30.4.en: Paul also stood to be tried before King Agrippa, and the king said: "Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian" (Acts 26:28).

11.31.0.en: "The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life; and he that winneth souls is wise" [30]

11.31.1.en: Men of God offer the fruit of righteousness as a tree of life, from which sinners pluck and are refreshed and live. They offer not abstract theoretical teachings, but the word of God, the giver of life. In this they win souls for the account of the Kingdom of God.

11.31.2.en: This is what the children of God seek, imitating the Apostle Paul, who wished to win the souls of all mankind. "For though I be free from all men, yet have I made myself servant unto all, that I might gain the more. And unto the Jews I became as a Jew, that I might gain the Jews; to them that are under the law, as under the law, that I might gain them that are under the law... I am made all things to all men, that I might by all means save some" (1 Cor 9:19-22).

11.32.0.en: "Behold, the righteous shall be recompensed in the earth: much more the wicked and the sinner" [31]

11.32.1.en: If the life we live is full of weaknesses, so that even the righteous and the just who will be rewarded in heaven are not spared from trials and afflictions, because of the weakness of their nature and their falling into sins, how much more must the wicked and sinners who persist in their evils and obstinacy expect eternal troubles and a terrible fate!

11.32.2.en: * "If the righteous scarcely be saved, where shall the ungodly and the sinner appear?"... If God gives us anything, He will test our work by it, and who is justified except he who is purer than the sun? He who hates God is wicked. The "sinner" is he who walks in evil.

11.32.4.en: By Your righteousness lead me in all my life!

11.32.5.en: * All the scales have been upset before me because of my sins.

11.32.6.en: Who but You can restore to me the spirit of sincerity and balance?

11.32.7.en: In You I know how my soul is sanctified, and my body too!

11.32.8.en: In You my senses are in harmony with my mind, for my edification and glory!

11.32.9.en: In You I see everything as holy and blessed!

11.32.10.en: Take away from me the scales of deceit and false concepts.

11.32.11.en: * By Your righteousness I imitate You, O You who are meek and lowly in heart.

11.32.12.en: Pride cannot creep into me and destroy my life with folly.

11.32.13.en: * By Your righteousness I enjoy the spirit of uprightness, so that I do not turn to the right hand or to the left.

11.32.14.en: May crookedness not carry me to shame and disgrace!

11.32.15.en: * By Your righteousness I see You as my wealth and my treasure!

11.32.16.en: You satisfy me, and water me, and enrich me, and gladden my heart!

11.32.17.en: I do not rely on the wealth of the world and its treasures, for the world and all that is in it passes away.

11.32.18.en: And I remain with You in Your embrace forever.

11.32.19.en: May death not rule over me, and may the enemy of good find no place within me!

11.32.20.en: * I possess You, and so I possess perfection and security.

11.32.21.en: I walk in You, and my soul is filled with joy in hope.

11.32.22.en: You are my reward, my crown, and my glory!

11.32.23.en: * Let the whole world stand against me, for I am hidden in You, O Conqueror of the world!

11.32.24.en: The world hates me, because it hates You!

11.32.25.en: It devises plots against me, and perishes by them itself!

11.32.26.en: The world crucified You, and its authority was shattered!

11.32.27.en: It wanted to be rid of You, and the powers of darkness collapsed.

11.32.28.en: * You establish Your Kingdom within me.

11.32.29.en: You count me Your holy city.

11.32.30.en: No evil word is heard in it, nor unseemly jesting.

11.32.31.en: Rather, words of blessing go forth from my mouth.

11.32.32.en: There is not a word of contempt for my neighbor, but all hear Your words that give hope.

11.32.33.en: There is no tale-bearing nor betrayal of secrets, but every word is heard for edification.

11.32.34.en: * Your righteousness carries within it an inexpressible reward.

11.32.35.en: By it my soul is transformed into a bride adorned with Your grace.

11.32.36.en: And my soul is strengthened and made firm, so that the enemy does not steal my wealth; it bears Your icon, and knows nothing but love, tenderness and mercy!

11.32.37.en: Your righteousness bears fruit in the joyful fruits of the Spirit.

11.32.38.en: Your righteousness proclaims within me the pledge of eternal life.

11.32.39.en: Your righteousness makes my way straight, so that there is no crookedness in it; Your righteousness sanctifies my will, my feelings and my longings, so that I seek only good for every human being.

11.32.40.en: * My soul rejoices with the salvation of every soul.

11.32.41.en: I desire not only to give of the good things I have, but also to make myself a servant to all, that I may gain the more.

11.32.42.en: Let me give from what You have given me, for I have no merit in anything!

11.32.43.en: Let nothing occupy me in all my life but the winning of souls!
